_comment: Cell descriptor for layout/bin/compose-cell.py -- see layout/README.md
section 'Composing a gate' for the floorplan reasoning shared with every
other cell here, and layout/sampler_core/README.md for this cell's own
result and open items (issue #27 step 1 / issue #22).
sampler_core is design/sampler_core.spice's top-level subckt: xdut (one
ro_array_core instance) plus six sampler_dff instances (xsb/xsv/xsr1-
xsr4). This descriptor promotes layout/sampler_core-placement-poc/'s
own six-instance floorplan (unchanged: 55.66 um pitch, same sb/sv/
sr1-sr4 instance order/naming, same y=0.0 origin for every instance) to
a real, --check-reproducible cell recipe and adds this increment's
own new work: routing the shared vdd bus and shared vss bus across all
six sampler_dff instances.
Stage 'place' is the identical placement layout/sampler_core-placement
-poc/build.py already proved DRC-clean (132 devices, 79 nets) -- see
that directory's own README for the full floorplan derivation. This
descriptor additionally hand-declares, for each of the six instances,
the two ports the final stage needs: 'vdd' and 'vss', each landing
directly on that instance's own already-merged met1 rail (NOT a li1
gate pad needing a via-drop -- see layout/sampler_core/README.md's
'Where the vdd/vss ports land' section for the klayout.db measurement
that found this). Every declared port coordinate is in that BLOCK's
own local frame (x_um=0.0, the same local x for every instance since
all six reference the identical layout/sampler_dff/sampler_dff.gds
stream): y_um=7.0 for vdd (sampler_dff's own attic rail, met1/'metal2'
role, layer 68/20) and y_um=-3.5 for vss (its own basement rail, same
layer). 0.0 sits inside both rails' own measured x-span (vdd:
layout/sampler_dff/sampler_dff.gds itself) for every one of the six
instances, so no per-instance x offset is needed.
Stage 'route_supplies' wraps the whole six-instance placement as one
'core' block (from_stage: 'place', the same re-placement mechanic
layout/sampler_dff/cell.json's own 'route_supplies' stage and
layout/ro_array_core/cell.json's 'vddstub'/'vddbus'/'vssstub'/'vssbus'
stages already use), re-declares those twelve ports in the composed
cell's own GLOBAL frame (block offset + local x_um, i.e. x_um = i *
55.66 for each instance's own y=7.0/-3.5 point), and routes two
five-leg buses -- vdd chaining sb->sv->sr1->sr2->sr3->sr4 at y=7.0,
vss at the same chain at y=-3.5 -- each leg a plain 2-pin
'connectivity[]' entry with a same-height waypoint bridging the ~5.3 um
gap between adjacent instances' own bboxes, the same per-leg-entry
style (not a single N-pin bundle net) layout/sampler_dff/cell.json's
own 'route_supplies' stage already used for the identical reason: it
is portable across every klt build encountered in this repo's history,
including ones that silently drop an unrecognized 'legs[]' field
(klayout-tools#1548) rather than reject it.
Only vdd/vss are attempted this increment. clk/rst_n fan-out, the
ro_array_core instance and its wiring to the samplers' d pins, the
six d/q (plus en1-4/vddr1-4) top-level pin promotions, and whole-cell
klt lvs against design/sampler_core.spice's real .subckt sampler_core
all remain open -- see layout/sampler_core/README.md's 'What remains'
section. lvs below is expected to MISMATCH heavily this increment (no
ro_array_core instance placed yet, no clk/rst_n/d/q wiring at all) --
recorded as expected and documented, not treated as a regression, the
same convention layout/sampler_dff/cell.json's own first vdd/vss-only
increment (PR #78) used.
A compose-cell.py limitation found (not a klt gap) while wiring up
this lvs block, worth recording for whoever attempts the real
whole-cell LVS pass (issue #27 step 5): 'dependency_variants' repoints
renamed subckt calls (repoint_variant_instances) ONLY inside the TOP
subckt's own extracted lines (lvs.subckt); a plain 'dependencies'
entry's own body is emitted via build_reference alone, with no
repoint pass. ro_array_core is listed as a plain dependency here (it
is sampler_core's dependency, not its own top subckt in THIS
descriptor, unlike layout/ro_array_core/cell.json's own lvs block,
where it IS the top subckt and gets repointed correctly) -- so its
own 'xr1 ... ro_ring5 wstv=0.42 ...' instance lines still call the
bare, undefined 'ro_ring5' name even though only the renamed
'ro_ring5_r1'..'_r4' definitions exist in the generated reference.
klt lvs does not error on this (confirmed: it silently drops the
unresolvable instances rather than failing the run), which is why
this stays a MISMATCH-with-a-known-incomplete-reference rather than a
crash -- reference device count reads 176 here (6x sampler_dff's own
22 plus ro_array_core's 4 ro_buf + 3 xor2 devices only; its four
ro_ring5 instances' 132 devices are the ones silently dropped), not
the full 264 a fully-resolved reference would have. Confirmed by
grepping sampler_core.ref.spice directly: 'ro_ring5' (bare) appears
only on instance-call lines, never as a '.subckt' header. Fixing this
generically (extending repoint_variant_instances to every
dependencies[] entry's own body, not just the top subckt's) is real,
separable compose-cell.py work -- left for whoever attempts a genuine
LVS MATCH at this scope, since no match is claimed or needed by this
vdd/vss-only increment either way.

stages.name: route_ctrl
_comment: Issue #27 step 2 / issue #22: route the shared clk fan-out and the
shared rst_n fan-out across all six sampler_dff instances -- the
'What remains' item layout/sampler_core-placement-poc/README.md and
layout/sampler_core/README.md both flagged as likely the hardest
remaining step, by analogy with layout/sampler_dff/README.md's own
single-cell clk fan-out derivation (a five-pin bundle net inside one
cell). At THIS scope clk/rst_n are each already a single, already-
routed net *inside* every one of the six sampler_dff instances (see
layout/sampler_dff/cell.json's own clk_met1/clk_bus and
rst_n_met1/rst_n_bus stages), each carrying its own correctly-spelled
net-name text label as a side effect of that routing (confirmed
directly against layout/sampler_dff/sampler_dff.gds with
klayout.db: layer 69/20 ('metal3' role, physical met2) text labels
'clk' at local (3.662, -1.7) and 'rst_n' at local (27.645, 2.2)) --
so this stage's own job is the SAME chain-of-six technique
route_supplies above already used for vdd/vss, not a fresh
six-pin-bundle derivation from scratch.
Anchor points: local (25.0, -1.7) for clk and (27.0, 2.2) for
rst_n, both on layer 69/20 (met2, 'metal3' role), width_um 0.17 --
an INTERIOR point on each instance's own already-drawn met2 run,
not an edge pin, the same 'land directly on the target net's own
metal, no via needed' technique route_supplies used for vdd/vss
(there on met1/'metal2') and layout/sampler_dff/cell.json's own
m_met1/final stages used for the tg_fbm_b_alt anchor. clk's x=25.0
sits inside its own measured met2 span for every one of the six
instances (local x 0.46..49.115 per the clk_bus stage's own lane,
unchanged since PR #99/#84), and clk's own chain (below) routes
clean on the FIRST attempt at y=-1.7 -- that lane already spans the
cell's full local width (clk_bus's own _comment: 'below every
leaf's own drawn geometry ... The lane spans x 0.545..49.03'), so a
straight cross-instance haul at that same height never crosses
anything else.
rst_n is NOT that simple: its own in-cell bus (rst_n_bus, y=2.2)
spans only local x 12.215..43.075, by design -- clear of clk's own
verticals ONLY inside that window (rst_n_bus's own _comment: clk's
two ctrlb drops at x=24.6/29.74 stop at y=1.03/1.24, well below
rst_n's own y=1.975 lower edge). Outside that window, clk's OTHER
two verticals (tg_d.ctrl at local (5.31, 2.5), tg_fbs.ctrl at local
(49.03, 2.5)) reach well above rst_n's own height, and a first
attempt at this stage's own port x=25.0 (matching clk's, for a
uniform anchor) hit exactly that: gen-compose rejected all five
rst_n legs ('self-net's drawn 0.17um metal overlaps ... block
'core''s own drawn pad metal ... (ports 'sb_clk', 'sv_clk')') --
not because the PORT itself collided (25.0 is mid-span, clear at
y=2.2 in isolation), but because a straight y=2.2 haul from that
port all the way to the CELL EDGE (needed to reach the next
instance) crosses local x 43.9..49.1, where clk's own tg_fbs.ctrl
riser and (per klayout.db, layer 69/20) several OTHER nets' own
narrow met2 verticals live at that same height -- confirmed
directly: a y=2.15..2.25 band slice across the whole cell width
own bus (12.005-43.285) -- every one a different net's own
vertical, invisible to the naive 'is x inside rst_n's own labelled
span' check this stage's first attempt used.
Fix: route rst_n's cross-instance haul on a COMPLETELY empty met2
lane instead of reusing y=2.2 outside the cell's own rst_n_bus
span. A klayout.db band scan (thin y-slices, full local x -3..52)
found local y=3.4..6.9 entirely free of met2 in every one of the
six identical instances (nothing this repo has drawn there:
vdd's own rail starts at y=6.915, everything else -- clk, rst_n,
q/qb/s/mc/mb, the leaf gates' own vdd/ctrl pads -- tops out at or
below y=2.795). Also confirmed at the chosen anchor column
specifically (local x=27.0, inside rst_n's own 12.215..43.075
span and clear of BOTH ctrlb drops at 24.6/29.74): met2 there is
only rst_n's own lane (y 2.115..2.285) below y=2.285 and the clk
basement lane (y -1.785..-1.615) below that -- nothing between
2.285 and 7.1. So each leg vias nowhere (still landing directly on
already-drawn met2, no physical via) but climbs the SAME layer
from (27.0, 2.2) straight up to (27.0, 5.0) -- comfortably inside
the empty band -- runs the whole inter-instance haul at y=5.0,
then drops back down to (27.0, 2.2) at the next instance, via an
explicit four-point waypoints_um U-shape per leg (the same
recipe rst_n_bus's own in-cell stage already used at smaller
scale, just one plane 'higher' in y rather than crossing a plane
in layer). clk needed no such detour and keeps its own single
straight-line legs at y=-1.7 unchanged.
Global x per instance: clk = origin_x + 25.0 (sb=25.0, sv=80.66,
sr4=305.3) -- the same offset arithmetic route_supplies already
used for vdd/vss at x=0.0.
Ten two-pin connectivity[] entries (five legs each for clk/rst_n,
chaining sb->sv->sr1->sr2->sr3->sr4), each with an explicit
waypoints_um path -- not a single six-pin bundle net with
connectivity[].legs[], for the same portability reason
route_supplies's own _comment already gives (klayout-tools#1548:
an unrecognized legs[] field is silently dropped rather than
rejected on some installed klt builds encountered in this repo's
history).
Still open after this stage (issue #27 steps 3-6): placing a
ro_array_core instance and wiring its xo/ro1-ro4 outputs to the
samplers' d pins, the six d/q (plus en1-4/vddr1-4, vdd, vss)
top-level pin promotions, whole-cell klt lvs against
design/sampler_core.spice's real .subckt sampler_core, and
post-layout PVT simulation of the assembled, LVS-clean cell.
